summary.text: A 17-year-old boy had headache, nausea and vomiting starting two days before transfer from a peripheral centre to the stroke unit on the afternoon of the third day. Asthenia and fever were revealed on arrival; neurological examination showed drowsiness, left hemiparesis, bilateral sixth cranial nerve palsy, bilateral Babinski responses, absent corneal reflexes and small pupillary light reactions.

Pre-transfer CT showed cerebellar hypodensities and CTA a basilar artery top occlusion. Admission MRI showed right cerebellar and other DWI lesions with a pc-ASPECTS of 6-5 points, and MRA absent basilar flow. DSA showed thrombotic occlusion of the left vertebral artery near the PICA origin, thrombotic material probably due to focal dissection, and basilar apex occlusion.

After a multidisciplinary decision, ADAPT with an AXS Catalyst 6F aspiration catheter achieved complete recanalization, with normal posterior circulation after the second pass; end-of-procedure angiography showed a left vertebral dissection intimal flap. He went to intensive care, and a CT six hours later showed ventricular dilatation from cytotoxic oedema, treated with anti-edemigenic therapy including mannitol. After neurosurgical consultation a preventive occipital craniectomy was performed without complications.

At 24 hours the neurological state had improved, and CT twelve hours after craniectomy showed better lesion definition and improved ventricular size. Five days after the endovascular treatment he was alert with left upper limb hyposthenia and bilateral sixth nerve deficiency only. He remained stable, moved to another centre for rehabilitation one week after arrival and finished functioning normally with slight left upper limb hyposthenia.

Endovascular treatmentThe digital substraction angiogram (DSA) images demonstrate the various phases of treatment: a) an anteroposterior (AP) angiogram of the right vertebral artery shows the common origin (black arrow) of the artery with a costocervical trunk; b) AP angiograms of the left vertebral artery in the neck and intracranial areas show a focal length dissection of the proximal V2 trait (double black arrows) and (c) thrombotic occlusion (black arrow with dot) immediately adjacent to the origin of the posterior inferior cerebellar artery (PICA); d-e) AP and latero-lateral (LL) angiograms of the left vertebral artery after the first pass with the catalyst aspiration catheter show the basilar artery occluded at the apex (black arrowheads); f-g) AP and LL angiograms of the left vertebral artery after the second pass with the catalyst aspiration catheter demonstrate normal posterior circulation (modified thrombolysis in cerebral infarction (mTICI 3)); h) AP angiogram of the left vertebral artery in the neck shows the stability of the focal length dissection of the proximal V2 trait (black star) with a regular and orthograde flow.
